transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-07
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 63 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jenna Lowe (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (CTO - Nebula), Priya Kapoor (Head of MLOps - Nebula), Marco Ruiz (SRE - Nebula)

Summary: quick discovery to align on hosting options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), per-token economics, batching/caching levers for their chat assistant product, and pilot constraints (budget and timing).

00:00 Samir Patel: Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh quick agenda — we're gonna run through your current stack, what latency and budget targets are, and then Jenna's gonna cover some of the batching/caching levers and what a pilot looks like.
00:18 Liam Chen: Yeah thanks, um so I just wanna say, budget is tight for this quarter so we're leaning towards hosted if the unit economics work. We have some regulatory stuff, but not heavy residency needs yet.
00:29 Priya Kapoor: Also we have a mix of synchronous chat and async summarization. Typical chat is 2 to 6 turns, average 220 tokens per user request, maybe 1.8 qps steady across the day with 80 peak.
00:45 Jenna Lowe: Got it. That profile is helpful. A few clarifying q's: are you doing prefix caching today or any KV style caching?
00:53 Marco Ruiz: We have very minimal caching — just CDN for static assets. No prefix caching in model layer, we've tried some basic reuse but nothing production.
01:05 Samir Patel: Ok that plays into cost a lot — batching and prefix/KV caching can move the needle substantially on per-token cost. For Redwood hosted our baseline per-token is competitive, and for dedicated you get predictable throughput and lower unit price for high qps.
01:20 Liam Chen: Can you give a ballpark? Their pricing vs what we currently pay at Anthropic is a question.
01:26 Samir Patel: Sure, ballpark numbers in a pilot vary because of sequence length and batching, but typical hosted unit cost for a 2k-sequence generator could be 0.6 to 1.1x of what you see now depending on batching. Jenna, wanna explain batching effects?
01:39 Jenna Lowe: Yeah, so at 1.8 qps and avg 220 tokens, you can benefit from micro-batching within a 20-40ms window. If you accept a small added tail latency for a fraction of requests we can double batch efficiency and cut per-token compute cost by ~25-40% — and prefix caching for repeated prompts can add another 10-30% reduction. There's also quantized model variants that reduce GPU memory and improve throughput for lower precision use cases.
02:05 Priya Kapoor: When you say 'quantized variants' are you talking 4-bit/8-bit? We need to know the quality delta.
02:10 Jenna Lowe: Mostly 8-bit and Q4 compression options we've verified on common LLM architectures. Quality regression is workload dependent; we run a quick eval on a sample prompt set to validate. For chat assistant tasks we've seen negligible quality drop for many open models. We'll propose a short eval in the pilot.
02:29 Liam Chen: What about latency SLOs? Our product needs p95 under 500ms for core conversational flows or we can't ship.
02:35 Jenna Lowe: For hosted with inference-tuned kernels and small batching windows, hitting p95 under 500ms for 200-300 token responses is achievable. If you're within that bound and you still need cost savings, dedicated gives you stronger p95 guarantees because of reserved GPU pools and controlled co-tenancy.
02:52 Marco Ruiz: We have PCI scope starting next quarter so encryption and KMS is non-negotiable. Can Redwood host KMS keys or do we bring our own?
02:59 Samir Patel: We support customer-managed keys (bring your KMS/HSM) for Private deployments, and for Dedicated we offer integration with customer KMS for data-at-rest encryption. Hosted supports envelope encryption but for maximum control we usually recommend Private. We'll send the SOC2/KMS docs.
03:17 Priya Kapoor: Another ask — can we run a cost sensitivity table? Like if average tokens per request jumps to 400 or 600 how does unit cost change?
03:25 Jenna Lowe: Absolutely. We can run scenarios: with no prefix caching and minimal batching, then with progressive batching windows and with prefix cache enabled. We'll include model variant comparisons (baseline fp16 vs Q4/Q8).
03:36 Liam Chen: How long does a Dedicated commitment look like? We're not ready for long-term reserved capacity but we could try a 3-month pilot with committed baseline and burst credit.
03:45 Samir Patel: We often do 3-month pilots for dedicated-style pilots — it's a reserved baseline with burst buffer for spikes. That lets you validate throughput and unit economics before a larger commit.
03:55 Jenna Lowe: For the pilot benchmark, we'll run two runs: 1) sim of your traffic with KV cache off, 2) with cache on and batching tuned. We'll collect p50/p95/p99 and token cost. Also test fallback to a smaller model variant under load to keep latency SLOs.
04:12 Marco Ruiz: On the fallback — does Redwood have automatic fallback policies by route? We want to reserve capacity for top-level auth flows but degrade lower priority tasks.
04:20 Jenna Lowe: Yes, smart routing and per-route policies are supported — you can pin models per route, have canary rollouts, and specify fallback chains (e.g., full model -> quantized variant -> smaller model).
04:31 Liam Chen: Good. On the billing side, how granular are we billed? Per-token only or any minimums?
04:36 Samir Patel: Hosted is per-token with monthly invoice and usage dashboards. Dedicated has reserved capacity plus per-token for overages depending on the plan. We can show example invoices.
04:45 Priya Kapoor: Any hidden costs — like egress from model logging or KV cache storage fees?
04:49 Samir Patel: We keep logging reasonable; audit logs are part of the enterprise package sometimes with retention add-ons. KV cache storage is usually negligible because it's in-memory, but if you need persistent cache replication there may be storage costs — we'll call that out in the pricing sheet.
05:05 Liam Chen: Competitors we looked at offered aggressive per-token numbers but often required a 12-month commit. We want flexibility.
05:11 Samir Patel: That's a common tradeoff. We'll include a flex pilot option: shorter commit, slightly higher unit price, plus an option to convert to a reserved rate after the pilot.
05:21 Priya Kapoor: Ok can you walk through an example math for our numbers? 1.8 qps, avg 220 tokens, assume 30% cache hit and batching benefit 30%?
05:30 Jenna Lowe: Sure — rough calc: baseline compute tokens per minute = 1.8 qps * 220 tokens * 60 = ~23,760 tokens/min. With 30% prefix cache hit you only compute 70% = ~16,632 tokens/min. Batching and kernel efficiency might reduce compute cost per token by another 30% effectively — so your billed token equivalent could be down to about 11,600 tokens/min in effective compute units. We'll run a proper spreadsheet for line items (model cost, infra overhead, storage, networking).
06:00 Marco Ruiz: Are model weights stored per-tenant? For private deployments we need physical separation and full image isolation.
06:06 Jenna Lowe: Private gives you a customer-managed control plane and isolated runtime; yes weights can be deployed onto your VPC or on-prem with isolation guarantees and no shared repos.
06:15 Liam Chen: What's the usual ramp timeline from pilot to prod? We might want to go live on hosted first and then migrate to Dedicated or Private later.
06:22 Samir Patel: Typical path is Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private for customers that tighten controls. Ramp time varies but a Hosted pilot can be 2-3 weeks. Dedicated pilot with reserved infra and validation ~4-6 weeks. Private onboarding can add more time depending on network and KMS integration.
06:36 Priya Kapoor: We need to ensure data residency later too — can Redwood support EU-only regions?
06:41 Samir Patel: Yes we have region controls and can provision Dedicated and Private in EU regions. Hosted also has region routing options for requests.
06:48 Liam Chen: One more thing — do you surface per-route token cost in the console? We want to track which flows are burning the most.
06:54 Jenna Lowe: Yes, Redwood Console shows token-level cost per model/route and has trace hooks. You can set alerts when a route exceeds thresholds.
07:00 Samir Patel: Great — next steps: I'll send the pilot pricing & SOC2/KMS docs and Jenna will own the benchmark plan. Priya, you'll send traffic profiles.
07:08 Priya Kapoor: I'll get those over by Tuesday.
07:12 Marco Ruiz: We'll want the SE benchmark to run during a maintenance window — tentatively next Tuesday morning PST.
07:18 Jenna Lowe: Works for us. We'll sketch the test harness and share the script.
07:24 Liam Chen: For legal, we may need a data processing addendum; can you include a template?
07:29 Samir Patel: Yes we'll include DPA template in the follow-up pack.
07:33 Priya Kapoor: Quick Q — if during the pilot our average tokens jumps to 400, what's realistic cost delta?
07:37 Jenna Lowe: Rough sense: doubling average tokens doesn't double fixed overheads but increases compute proportionally; with caching and batching the marginal per-token cost still benefits from batching efficiency up to GPU memory limits. We'll model scenarios in the spreadsheet.
07:50 Liam Chen: Alright thanks that's helpful.
07:52 Samir Patel: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the items listed.
07:55 Meeting end.
